did i have any complications after surge.text:
Yes, one — and it resolved.

On [2026-04-28] you recorded that the wound was redder than before, warm to touch, with yellowish discharge at one end of the incision, and a temperature of 37.9. You rang the surgical team that morning.

You were seen the next day [2026-04-29], where it was identified as a **superficial wound infection**. A swab was taken and you started **cephalexin 500mg four times daily for seven days**, with instructions to come straight back if the redness spread or you developed a fever.

It improved quickly: redness had pulled back with no further discharge and a normal temperature by day five [2026-05-03], and you finished the course on [2026-05-06] with the wound looking clean.

Pain sat around 5/10 through that period [2026-05-06] before continuing to improve.
